title: E1 vocabulary checkpoint form A
instructions: Use the whole sentence to choose the most precise meaning. Complete all five before submitting the checkpoint.

parts.prompt: The announcement was ambiguous: one sentence said the hall would open at seven, while another suggested that registration ended at seven. What does “ambiguous” most nearly mean?

options.text: open to more than one interpretation

choice_rationales.A: The two statements permit conflicting interpretations.
choice_rationales.D: The announcement is being read, not heard.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Ambiguous language has more than one possible meaning and is therefore unclear.

parts.prompt: The speaker gave a compelling explanation, combining clear data with examples that answered the audience's doubts. What does “compelling” most nearly mean?

choice_rationales.A: The explanation answers doubts rather than remaining incomplete.
choice_rationales.C: Data and relevant examples make the case persuasive.
choice_rationales.D: Convincing evidence does not make a claim unquestionable.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Compelling means powerfully convincing, not necessarily beyond all challenge.

parts.prompt: The first route saved only twelve seconds over a forty-minute journey, so the coach considered the advantage negligible. What does “negligible” most nearly mean?

choice_rationales.A: The time has already been calculated.
choice_rationales.B: Twelve seconds is insignificant beside forty minutes.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Negligible means so slight that it is not worth considering.

parts.prompt: Instead of using the conventional method taught in the manual, Mei tested a new arrangement of the equipment. What does “conventional” most nearly mean?

choice_rationales.A: The manual's established method contrasts with the new arrangement.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Conventional describes what follows established practice.

parts.prompt: Before approving the totals, the treasurer scrutinised every receipt and compared it with the electronic record. What does “scrutinised” most nearly mean?

choice_rationales.A: The receipts are used as evidence.
choice_rationales.B: The electronic comparison is not based on memory.
choice_rationales.C: Checking every receipt against another record requires close examination.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Scrutinised means inspected carefully and thoroughly.
